text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Searches were carried out on the premises of Tauras Bank after its chairman, 52-year-old Genadijus Konopliovas, was found dead on Monday with a bullet wound to the head. Police suspect suicide.
LIETUVOS RYTAS

- U.S. deputy assistant state secretary Ron Asmus held the initial round of talks with Lithuanian diplomats about the Baltic Charter. The document, which is expected to be signed in autumn, has no security guarantees but is aimed at convincing the Baltic states that the U.S. sees therm as fully-fledged members of the West.
- Parliament decided that banks will have to insure the deposits in all European Union currencies from January 1 1998.

- Lithuanian Pressident Algirdas Brazauskas continues to lead public opinion polls ahead of December's presidential race. The chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis was ranked fourth, following U.S. E.P.A. bureaucrat Valdas Admkus and former prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas, a poll conducted by Vilmorus said.
- Snoras Bank decided to boost its share capital to 27 million litas from 20 million litas. It is expected that the current shareholders will buy the major part of the issue.
- Societe Generale European Emerging Markets intends to become one of the major foreign players in Lithuania's financial market.
RESPUBLIKA
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said in an interview to the newspaper that he expects the state-run Savings Bank to run more effeciently after the whole board was changed last week.
- Parliament approved the draft resolution to abolish capital punishment.
- The Bank of Lithuania decided to hold repo auctions on the eighth of July, August and September.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- Union Bank of Switzerland said it was eyeing the Lithuanian market.
VERSLO ZINIOS
- Investment Bank Williams De Broe and Lithuanian brokerage house Vilfima will distribute eight million litas of Hermis Bank shares as global depository receipts.
- The revised foreign trade deficit of Lithuania was 4.816 billion litas in 1996.
- The volume of retail trade was 4.9 billion litas in the first five months of the year.
- Creditanstalt Investment Bank will compete to become a lead advisor to the country's government for Telecom privatisation. -- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 22 35 17
